definitions.gloss: osechi; traditional Japanese New Year dishes
definitions.explanation: Traditional Japanese cuisine prepared for the New Year celebration, consisting of various dishes with symbolic meanings, typically served in special lacquered boxes.

examples.japanese: {元日|がんじつ}の{朝|あさ}、おせち{料理|りょうり}を{食|た}べた。
examples.english: On New Year's morning, I ate osechi dishes.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}はおせちを{自分|じぶん}で{作|つく}ってみた。
examples.english: This year I tried making osechi myself.

examples.japanese: デパートでおせちを{予約|よやく}した。
examples.english: I ordered osechi from a department store.

notes:
FULL FORM:
おせち{料理|りょうり} (osechi ryouri) is the full term.

COMMON DISHES:
・{黒豆|くろまめ} (black soybeans - for health)
・{数|かず}の{子|こ} (herring roe - for fertility)
・{栗|くり}きんとん (sweet chestnuts - for wealth)
・{伊達巻|だてまき} (rolled omelet - for learning)
・{紅白|こうはく}かまぼこ (fish cake - good fortune)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Osechi dishes are designed to be prepared in advance and eaten cold over the first few days of the New Year, allowing families to rest from cooking.
